bill.name: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to limit the number of terms an individual may serve as a Member of Congress (S.J. Res. 48)
bill.status: Introduced in Senate · McCormick · read twice and referred to Judiciary on 2025-04-10
bill.analyzed: Full introduced-in-Senate joint resolution (2 pages; proposed article §§1–3 and ratification condition)

sourceLimits: The supplied 1,824-byte, 316-word raw source is a flattened, single-line extraction of the introduced-in-Senate joint resolution. It contains the ratification condition and the complete three-section proposed article, but it has no page boundaries or metadata sidecar and omits the standard resolving formula's statement that two-thirds of each House must concur. The separately checked official PDF supplies that language and establishes the two-page count; Congress.gov actions metadata still records only introduction and referral to the Senate Committee on the Judiciary on April 10, 2025. The measure proposes a constitutional rule rather than an ordinary statutory program. It assigns no implementing or reporting body, prescribes no eligibility-administration or dispute procedure, appropriates no funds, requires no recurring data product, and states no downstream purpose or measurable outcome beyond the service limits, partial-term rules, and pre-118th-Congress exclusion. Its term counts, partial-term thresholds, ratification threshold, and seven-year window are legal design parameters or adoption gates rather than outcome series. A State-ratification count would be an objectively checkable one-time legal milestone, but at the introduced stage there is no submission date or fixed ratification deadline, and the sources establish no recurring official series or named resolver for a downstream outcome. Forecasting that the limits apply conditional on ratification would merely restate the proposed article. Effects on turnover, experience, electoral competition, representation, legislative performance, or public trust are not stated in the text and are not inferred. Accordingly, this extraction has one provision and three literal legal goals, but zero forecastable metrics, stance matrices, series hints, or empirical conditionals.

provisions.title: Proposed constitutional article — Sections 1–3
provisions.heading: Congressional term limits, partial-term counting, and the pre-118th-Congress exclusion
provisions.quote: “No person shall serve as a Representative for more than six two-year terms.” … “No person shall serve as a Senator for more than two six-year terms.” … “This article shall not apply to any person who served as a Representative or as a Senator during any Congress occurring before the One Hundred Eighteenth Congress.”
provisions.context:
S.J. Res. 48 proposes one constitutional article rather than an ordinary statutory program. The separately checked official PDF's resolving formula requires two-thirds of each House to concur before submission. After submission, the article would become part of the Constitution only if the legislatures of three-fourths of the States ratified it within seven years. Section 1 sets a six-term House limit and treats service exceeding one year of a two-year term as a complete term. Section 2 sets a two-term Senate limit and treats service exceeding three years of a six-year term as a complete term. Both deeming rules apply whether or not the person was originally elected to the term. Section 3 says that the entire article shall not apply to any person who served in either chamber during a Congress before the 118th Congress. The text limits service rather than expressly regulating candidacy or election and supplies no enforcement clause.

Source limits / honesty note: The raw text and official bill metadata state no downstream objective, administrator, enforcement process, appropriation, report, or recurring data product. The numerical caps and ratification thresholds are legal rules and adoption gates, not forecastable outcome series. This extraction therefore does not infer changes in turnover, tenure, elections, representation, legislative performance, or public trust, and it leaves metrics, series hints, stance matrices, and empirical conditionals empty.
goals: Limit each covered person's service as a Representative to no more than six two-year terms, treating service exceeding one year in a term as a complete term whether or not the person was originally elected to it.

Limit each covered person's service as a Senator to no more than two six-year terms, treating service exceeding three years in a term as a complete term whether or not the person was originally elected to it.
Exclude from the article any person who served as a Representative or Senator during a Congress before the 118th Congress.

effects.text: The proposed article would have no constitutional effect unless two-thirds of each House concurred in its submission and three-fourths of the State legislatures ratified it within seven years after submission.

effects.mechanism: House service cap and partial-term rule
effects.text: If ratified, Section 1 would prohibit a covered person from serving as a Representative for more than six two-year terms and would deem service exceeding one year of any such term to be a complete term, including service by someone other than the person originally elected.

effects.mechanism: Senate service cap and partial-term rule
effects.text: If ratified, Section 2 would prohibit a covered person from serving as a Senator for more than two six-year terms and would deem service exceeding three years of any such term to be a complete term, including service by someone other than the person originally elected.

Section 3 says the article shall not apply to any person with House or Senate service during any Congress before the 118th Congress. On its face, the exclusion attaches to the entire article rather than merely disregarding pre-118th-Congress terms; this extraction records that textual scope without predicting how a chamber or court would resolve any dispute.

barriers.text: The analyzed measure remains introduced and has not been submitted for ratification. Two-thirds of each House must first concur, and then three-fourths of the State legislatures must ratify within a seven-year clock that does not begin until submission.

barriers.actor: The House, Senate, election administrators, and adjudicators
barriers.text: The proposed article prohibits service and supplies two partial-term deeming rules, but it does not assign an administrator or specify ballot, credentialing, seating, challenge, recordkeeping, or enforcement procedures. It also does not state how service of exactly one year in a House term or exactly three years in a Senate term should be counted.
